d: In the foreground is King Heinrich under a mighty old oak (court oak), first there are Saxon and Thuringian counts, noble and rice, which form the king's army banner. Opposite are the Brabantian counts and nobles, rice and people, at their head Frederick of Telramund, to whose side Ortrud. The center forms an open circle. The army caller of the king and four hornwinds walk into the middle. The wind blows the king's cry.

Elsa appears in a white, very simple garment; she lingers in the background for a while, then she moves very slowly and with great shame towards the middle of the foreground; women, dressed very simply white, follow her, but these remain in the background at the extreme limit of the court circle.

In the castle of Antwerp. In the middle of the background of the Palas (Ritterwohnung), on the left in the foreground the Kemenate (female apartment); on the right in the foreground the gate of the Münster; on the right in the background the tower gate. It is night. The windows of the Palas are brightly lit; from the Palas one hears jubilant music, horns and trombones sound funny. On the steps to the Münster gate Friedrich and Ortrud sit, both in dark, poor clothing. Ortrud, the arms supported on his knees, clings her eye unwalled to the bright windows of the Palas; Friedrich looks darkly to the earth.
Elsa, dressed in white, appears on the Söller; she steps on the parapet and leans her head on her hand

After seeing the place, which could hide it most advantageously from the people, he steps behind a rampart of the Münster. Gradual dawn. Two guards blow the morning song from the tower; one hears the answer from a more distant tower. As the towerers descend and open the gate, servicemen arise from different directions of the castle, greet them, go to rest at their directions, etc. Some draw water at the fountain in metal vessels, knock on the gate of the pala and are let in with it. The gate of the pala opens again, the four hornwinds of the king walk out and blow the call, then they step back into the pala. The servicemen have left the stage. From the castle courtyard and through the tower gate, numerous brabantic nobles and men come together in front of the cathedral; they welcome themselves in cheerful excitement.

A long train of women in magnificent robes slowly steps out of the gate of the Kemenate onto the Söller; he turns left on the main path past the Palas and from there again to the front of the Münster, on whose steps the first ones to come stand up.
The king, Lohengrin, and the Saxon Counts and Nobles have stepped out of the palace in solemn procession; the train is interrupted by the confusion in the foreground.
The bridal chamber, in the middle of the background the richly decorated bridal bed; in an open bay window a low resting bed. Music behind the scene; the singing is only distant, then approaching.

Elsa is, when the trains have left the chamber; how exuberant Lohengrin sunk to the chest. Lohengrin sits down on the sleeping bed at the bay window while the singing fades away, pulling Elsa gently after him.

The floodplain on the bank of the Scheldt, as in Act I. Bright dawn, gradually dawning on the full day. A count with his entourage ascends to the right in the foreground, rising from the horse and handing it over to a servant. Two noble boys carry his shield and spear. He plantes his banner, his entourage gathers around the same. While a second count moves in the way the first one approaches, one hears the trumpets of a third one. A third count moves in with his entourage as well. The new flocks gather around their banners; the counts and nobles greet, test and praise their weapons, etc. A fourth count moves in with his entourage from the right and rises up to the middle of the background. When the king's trumpets are heard from the left, everything rushes around the banners.
